corrected_value.title: Interpersonal forgiving in close relationships: II. Theoretical Elaboration and Measurement.

decisions.location: Abstract, line 1 (p. 1); Results, line 1 (pp. 11-12); Discussion, line 1 (p. 19); References, line 1 (p. 22)
decisions.quote: We took initial steps to partially replicate some of the work by McCullough et al. (1998) by including the revenge measure in our replication, yet we see the value in a more comprehensive revisiting of their study.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. In addition to using the TRIM avoidance and revenge subscales developed in McCullough et al. (1998) (Study 1), the authors empirically re-tested the negative correlation between forgiveness and revenge motivation (Hypothesis 2bii, r(261) = -0.43, p < .001—a relationship not tested in the 1997 paper, as indicated by '/' in Table 9) and whether forgiveness is more strongly linked with avoidance and revenge motivation than empathy (Hypothesis 2c), explicitly stating in the Discussion that 'We took initial steps to partially replicate some of the work by McCullough et al. (1998) by including the revenge measure in our replication' and in the Abstract that 'Overall, this was a successful replication of the findings by McCullough et al. (1997; 1998) with the empathy model of forgiveness receiving strong empirical support.' Shipped row 2257 (10.1037/0022-3514.73.2.321, JPSP 73(2), 321-336) is the earlier 1997 article by McCullough, Worthington, and Rachal, whereas McCullough et al. (1998) (10.1037/0022-3514.75.6.1586, JPSP 75(6), 1586-1603) is a separate multi-study follow-up article with additional co-authors and new empirical data rather than an alternate report of the 1997 study.
